T2-FLAIR Mismatch Present is absent, which argues against the classic IDH-mutant astrocytoma imaging signature. Evidence against IDH-wildtype includes Tumor Location and Region Proportions showing frontal/cortical/insular involvement and Cortical involvement being present, which can be seen with IDH-mutant gliomas, plus Enhancement Quality, ET Volume (mL), Proportion Enhancing, and NCR Volume (mL) showing only mild/minimal enhancing and necrotic tumor burden. Overall, the age and infiltrative multifocal/ependymal pattern outweigh the low-enhancement features, so the best estimate is IDH-wildtype.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structured conventional MRI metadata. Confidence is limited by absence of diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy, susceptibility/calcification assessment, and molecular testing. The very large FLAIR/edema-dominant infiltrative abnormality with tiny enhancing/necrotic volumes is somewhat atypical for classic enhancing glioblastoma, but the age, multifocal/bilateral distribution, deep white matter invasion, and ependymal involvement support an aggressive IDH-wildtype diagnosis.

who_grade.reasoning: For CNS WHO grade, the metadata favor grade 4 over grades 2 or 3 because Multifocal or Multicentric, Number of lesions, Side of Tumor Epicenter, Edema crosses midline, Deep WM invasion, Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion, ED Volume (mL), Total tumor volume (mL), and whole_tumor_sphericity indicate a very extensive, infiltrative, bilateral/multifocal tumor with ventricular and deep white matter involvement, an aggressive pattern most compatible with highest-grade diffuse glioma. Additional support comes from Enhancement Quality, Thickness of enhancing margin, ET Volume (mL), NCR Volume (mL), Proportion Enhancing, and Proportion Necrosis showing at least some enhancing/necrotic component, although small. Evidence against grade 4 is that Enhancement Quality is only mild, ET Volume (mL) and Proportion Enhancing are extremely low, NCR Volume (mL) is very small, and midline_shift_present with Asymmetrical Ventricles does not show marked mass effect. Weighing the aggressive distribution and invasion against the limited enhancement/necrosis, the best estimate is CNS WHO grade 4 rather than grade 3 or 2.
